territory: New York, London, Antwerp, Jerusalem and Bnei Brak (global urban diaspora)

population_unit: persons described as everyday users
population_definition: UCL project directly states around 700,000 Hasidic Jews use the variety as an everyday language; approximate global figure without territory split.
population_secondary_context: Not a census and not assignable to Stamford Hill, Salford or Canada. Source explicitly distinguishes CHY from prewar Eastern dialects and Standard Yiddish.
education_language_exposure_mismatch_by_: Same-script/register mismatch: children may learn the Hebrew alphabet through sacred Hebrew words they do not understand; Yiddish spelling may be taught later or never separately; Biblical Hebrew is taught via Yiddish translation without explicit Hebrew grammar/vocabulary.
learning_completion_evidence: Salford school evidence: 2016 enrolment 264, all bilingual/most Yiddish L1; after phonics revision Year 1 screening reached 90%. 2026 enrolment 215; nursery nearly entirely Yiddish, English phonics/writing began mid-Reception and some gaps persisted to school exit. Different cohorts/frameworks: not a trend or causal effect.
functional_resource_access: School phonics sequence is direct functional delivery evidence. Generic Yiddish corpora/speech exist but variant metadata/CHY compatibility is not established.

academic_lingua_franca_nonoverlap: Direct register evidence distinguishes understood Yiddish vernacular from high-prestige Hebrew text; school evidence shows delayed English academic foundations for many pupils, without attributing cause to Yiddish.

accessible_offline_delivery_evidence: Exact school print/phonics delivery is functional; open, accessible and offline CHY academic ladders remain unverified.
